quote: Side Letter § 1.1: Redefines "Territory" for purposes of the Side Letter to mean "Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, **New York and Virginia**." ... Distribution Agreement § 19.4: Order of precedence—Side Letter ranks above the body of the Agreement. ... The non-compete binds the Company ... in New York and Virginia—states where the Company has no distribution rights ... the 18-month post-termination non-compete continues to apply in all six states. ... Consider whether to seek a waiver or narrowing of the Side Letter's Territory as part of the Velloran consent negotiation
reason: Issue 4 of the memo identifies each element of the criterion. It names the Side Letter's redefinition of Territory to add NY and VA and cites the §19.4 precedence clause. It shows the non-compete reaching six states, including the 18-month post-term tail, while the Company's distribution rights cover only the original four. Its fix is to narrow the Side Letter Territory, which in substance means conforming the definition to the Distribution Agreement.
